items.title: Voyager 1 entering interstellar space
items.claim: Voyager 1 launched in 1977. When did NASA conclude it had crossed into interstellar space?

options.text: Around August 2012, confirmed by NASA in 2013

items.reveal:
Plasma density measurements from the Plasma Wave Subsystem confirmed the crossing.

Voyager 1 still transmits data; its plutonium power source will deplete in the mid-2020s to early 2030s.
items.why: Defining 'interstellar' requires a physical boundary, the heliopause, not a fixed distance.

items.title: The Milky Way and Andromeda
items.claim: Andromeda (M31) is moving toward the Milky Way at about 110 km/s. When are current models predicting first close passage?
items.reveal_title: Around 4.5 billion years, plus or minus
items.reveal:
Cox and Loeb (2008) predicted a close passage around 4.5 billion years from now, with full merger over subsequent billions of years.

Gaia data have refined Andromeda's tangential motion since.
items.why: Galactic-scale events follow timescales that dwarf human history.

items.title: JWST launch and arrival
items.claim: The James Webb Space Telescope launched on 25 December 2021. About how long to reach its operating point at L2?

options.text: About 30 days for L2 insertion; first science images released July 2022

items.reveal_title: About a month to L2; six months of commissioning before first science
items.reveal:
JWST inserted into L2 orbit on 24 January 2022. The first science images were released 12 July 2022.

The Sun-Earth L2 point lies about 1.5 million km from Earth.
items.why: Headline 'launch day' obscures months of staging required to make a telescope work.
